ko.text: The ED opens with all Must items

name: Hospital Emergency Department
tagline: An extension built during full operation, plus triage software
scope: Building a new emergency department extension while the hospital runs at full capacity, plus medical equipment and patient triage software connected to the hospital information system.
intro: You're running construction of a new emergency department. Meanwhile the hospital runs at full tilt – doctors have no time, patients mustn't suffer, and the region watches every penny.
predWorld: Construction during operation, medical equipment from public tenders, occupancy approval and hygiene standards.
agileWorld: Patient triage software and a dispatch screen, tuned with doctors and nurses on simulated shifts.

dependency.lock: Waiting for the network and equipment in the extension to go live (milestone)
dependency.hint: Pilot operation in the new premises waits for a predictive milestone – the network and equipment going live.

workstreams.name: Extension built during hospital operation
workstreams.why: Building permit, stages set around hospital operations, and fixed dependencies.

workstreams.name: Medical equipment via public tender
workstreams.why: Procurement law prescribes the procedure and deadlines; the specification must be done up front.

workstreams.name: Occupancy approval and hygiene standards
workstreams.why: Requirements are set by regulations and checked formally.

workstreams.name: Interface to the hospital information system
workstreams.why: Careful, even though it's software: the interface is defined by a standard and a contract with the system vendor, and it's tested formally.

workstreams.name: Patient triage software
workstreams.why: How triage should work in real operation only shows up on simulated shifts with doctors and nurses.

workstreams.name: ED dispatch screen
workstreams.why: What the screen needs is tuned with staff bit by bit.

workstreams.name: Staff training on new procedures
workstreams.why: Training is tuned in simulations based on where staff make mistakes – iteratively.

workstreams.name: Wait time info for patients
workstreams.why: A small service you can launch early and improve based on reactions.

backlog.name: Pilot operation in the new premises

milestones.name: Network and equipment
milestones.okText: The network and equipment in the extension are up. Pilot operation can be prepared from sprint 3.
milestones.lateText: Construction slipped. Pilot operation can't be prepared until sprint 4.

milestones.name: Occupancy approval
milestones.okText: The extension has passed occupancy approval.
milestones.lateText: Occupancy approval is postponed. The region is unhappy.

milestones.name: ED opening
milestones.okText: The new emergency department is open and the software is triaging its first patients.
milestones.lateText: The ED opened, but without key features:

shift.title: Software is a medical device
shift.text: The State Institute for Drug Control has ruled: software that ranks patients by urgency is a medical device. It can't be used without technical documentation, risk analysis and change control. Revealed factor: regulation and audits.
shift.lesson: When part of the agile work becomes a regulated product, formal elements must enter the agile part: a strict Definition of Done with documentation, and change control. Still agile, but with rules.

gate.title: Regional review
gate.text: The region, as the hospital's founder, checks whether the project is on plan and on budget. What do you present?
gate.lesson: A public founder needs transparency: the state of construction and budget, plus proof that the software really works in operation.

choices.text: Construction and budget status + video of a simulated shift with the software
choices.feedback: The region sees where the money goes and that the software helps doctors.

choices.text: Only construction figures; the software once it's done
choices.feedback: The region asks why it's paying for software nobody has seen.

choices.text: Postpone the review – too busy
choices.feedback: The region sends its own inspector.

events.title: Construction disturbs patients
events.text: Construction noise is disturbing ICU patients. The head physician demands an immediate stop.
events.lesson: Building during operation means planning work around operations – and talking to people before they complain upstairs.

choices.text: Noisy work only outside surgeries and quiet hours; offer patients other rooms
choices.feedback: The head physician agrees. Construction is slower, but conflict-free.

choices.text: Continue as planned
choices.feedback: Construction rolls on. So do the complaints.

choices.text: Stop noisy work for two weeks
choices.feedback: Peace in the ICU, but construction slips.

events.title: Doctors have no time to test
events.text: Doctors and nurses are fully booked on shifts. There's no time left to test software.
events.lesson: Without real users, agile development loses its point. Their time must be negotiated and paid for.

choices.text: Negotiate paid hours for simulated shifts with management
choices.feedback: Staff test on simulated shifts. It's expensive, but you see real use.

choices.text: Test without them, just in IT
choices.feedback: Tests pass. On paper.

choices.text: Test with one willing doctor
choices.feedback: Better than nothing, but one view isn't enough.

events.title: System vendor stalls the interface
events.text: The hospital system vendor wants double for the interface and won't deliver it for eight weeks.
events.lesson: Dependency on an external system is handled by contract and technically (a simulator). Bending the rules with medical data is a gamble.

choices.text: Lock the interface by contract per the standard; develop against a simulator meanwhile
choices.feedback: The interface is pricey but certain. Development doesn't stop.

choices.text: Bypass the interface with direct database access
choices.feedback: Works right away, for free. For now.

choices.text: Wait eight weeks
choices.feedback: Safe, but slow.

events.title: Flu epidemic
events.text: The hospital is overcrowded and wants to use the finished part of the extension as a temporary ward.
events.lesson: A crisis request goes through change control: what can be safely handed over now and what gets replanned.

choices.text: Hand over the finished part temporarily per the crisis plan; replan the rest
choices.feedback: The hospital handled the surge and construction continues in a new order.

choices.text: Refuse – construction has its plan
choices.feedback: Hospital management is furious. Patients lie in the corridors.

choices.text: Hand over the whole unfinished extension
choices.feedback: Help arrived instantly. Builders now work among patients.

events.title: Tender challenged
events.text: A losing bidder challenged the medical equipment tender at the competition authority.
events.lesson: Public procurement risks belong in the risk register with a ready plan B. Ignoring the authority doesn't pay.

choices.text: Activate plan B from the risk register: rent equipment temporarily
choices.feedback: Rented equipment bridges the wait for the authority's ruling.

choices.text: Wait for the authority's ruling
choices.feedback: The authority will rule in two months.

choices.text: Sign the contract anyway
choices.feedback: The equipment is ordered. The authority hasn't ruled yet.

events.title: Nurses want bedside tablets
events.text: Nurses want the software to work on bedside tablets too. It wasn't in the brief.
events.lesson: A new user request goes into the backlog and the Product Owner orders it. Building it on the side, off-plan, breaks the sprint.

choices.text: Into the backlog; the head nurse orders it and tests it on one shift
choices.feedback: One shift showed a simplified view is enough. Small effort, big payoff.

choices.text: Build it now, off-plan
choices.feedback: The sprint fell apart and the tablet version is half-baked.

choices.text: Refuse – it's not in the brief
choices.feedback: Nurses feel nobody listens to them.

stiznost.title: Complaint to the region
stiznost.text: Patients and the head physician complain to the regional authority. The region has announced a construction inspection.
stiznost.lesson: An ignored stakeholder conflict comes back through their bosses – and worse.
stiznost.unresolvedText: Complaints about the construction hurt the hospital's reputation.

choices.text: Admit the mistake, adjust the noisy-work schedule and inform patients
choices.feedback: The inspection went calmly. Relations are slowly mending.

choices.text: Argue that construction complies with the permit
choices.feedback: Formally true, but the region won't forget.

choices.text: Stop noisy work entirely
choices.feedback: Quiet, but a big slip.

odmitnuti.title: Nurses reject the software
odmitnuti.text: During the pilot, nurses refuse to use the software: it doesn't fit real operations and slows them down.
odmitnuti.lesson: Software tested without real users fails in operation. Feedback is cheaper early on.
odmitnuti.unresolvedText: Staff work around the software and keep paper lists.

choices.text: Stop the pilot, run simulated shifts with nurses and rework key screens
choices.feedback: After two iterations, nurses say: “Now this works.”

choices.text: Order them to use it
choices.feedback: Nurses fill in the software for show; the real queue is on paper.

choices.text: Keep the pilot running and collect feedback
choices.feedback: There are a hundred comments. Some contradict each other.

simulace_bonus.title: Nurses want more
simulace_bonus.text: Simulated shifts paid off. Nurses come up with ideas on their own and want the software launched sooner.
simulace_bonus.lesson: User involvement is an investment: people who co-create a solution then champion it themselves.
simulace_bonus.unresolvedText: Staff recommend the software to other departments on their own.

choices.text: Make the most active nurses ambassadors for other shifts
choices.feedback: Training the other shifts almost runs itself.

choices.text: Launch the whole software now, unfinished
choices.feedback: The enthusiasm faded fast.

choices.text: Say thanks and continue as planned
choices.feedback: A somewhat missed opportunity.

unik.title: Unauthorized access to patient data
unik.text: A security audit found direct access to the patient database outside the approved interface.
unik.lesson: Bending the rules on sensitive data is a project's most expensive “saving”. Incidents get reported and handled openly.
unik.unresolvedText: Unauthorized access to patient data came to light only after the opening.

choices.text: Block the access immediately, report the incident and build the interface properly
choices.feedback: Painful but honest. The authority appreciated the quick response.

choices.text: Keep quiet and remove the access on the sly
choices.feedback: The audit logged it anyway. Now it's a cover-up too.

choices.text: Block it and wait for the official interface
choices.feedback: Safe, but the software now has no data for weeks.

dodelavky.title: Finishing work among patients
dodelavky.text: Finishing work in the temporarily used extension clashes with operations: hygiene inspectors threaten a fine.
dodelavky.lesson: Handing over unfinished work without a punch-list plan means the problems move into operations.
dodelavky.unresolvedText: Unfinished work in the extension dragged on for months after the opening.

choices.text: Draw up a punch-list plan with operations and work section by section
choices.feedback: Slower, but no clash with the hygiene inspectors.

choices.text: Finish it fast over a weekend
choices.feedback: Sloppy work and exhausted tradespeople.

choices.text: Pay the fine and carry on
choices.feedback: The problem remains, just pricier.

zruseni.title: Authority voids the contract
zruseni.text: The competition authority canceled the tender. The ordered equipment must be returned and re-tendered.
zruseni.lesson: Getting ahead of the authority's ruling is a bet. Plan B from the risk register would have saved months here.
zruseni.unresolvedText: The ED opened with temporary equipment.

choices.text: Rent equipment temporarily and re-run the tender properly
choices.feedback: Expensive, but the ED opens on time.

choices.text: Sue the authority
choices.feedback: The lawsuit will outlast the whole project.

choices.text: Open without the new equipment
choices.feedback: The ED works only halfway.
